trade_setups.thesis: Nine of 18 FOMC officials projected a 2026 rate hike; the 2026 median rose to 3.8%; the easing bias was stripped. The 30Y closed at 4.94% — 6 bps from the 5.00% regime trigger. Retail sales at +0.9% (vs +0.5% expected) reinforces the sticky-inflation narrative. The FOMC has moved from 'zero cuts' to 'potential hike' — that repricing is worth 10-20 bps on the 30Y from current levels. TBT converts a defensive cash position into an active trade in the STEP_ASIDE regime.

bear_case: Nine hike dots at a 4.2% CPI backdrop signals a regime shift that has not fully repriced equities: SPX at 22x forward P/E with a 3.8% 2026 median rate and no easing bias implies 4-7% downside to fair value (~7,100-7,200), and the DXY at 99.65 and 30Y at 4.94% represent 35-bps and 6-bps proximity to dual regime breaches that would justify an outright BEARISH call. Strong retail sales at +0.9% versus a 0.5% consensus proves the consumer has not responded to 3.50-3.75% funds rate, which means the Fed must do more; Warsh's deliberate policy ambiguity — withholding his own dot, announcing a dot-plot review — creates the worst possible backdrop for equity multiples: neither certainty about the rate path nor a clear signal on when policy normalizes. If DXY closes above 100.10 AND 30Y closes above 4.98% on the same Thursday session, STEP_ASIDE upgrades to BEARISH. If SPX reclaims 7,460 on a daily close following a successful Iran signing on June 19 AND DXY falls below 99.00, STEP_ASIDE reverts to HOLD.
